title: Linear Equations & Inequalities
description: Solve multi-step linear equations, represent inequalities on a number line, and apply both skills to word problems.

notes.heading: Solving Multi-Step Linear Equations
notes.body:
📌 Definition
A linear equation is an equation where the highest power of the variable is 1.

🔑 How it works
To solve a multi-step equation, undo operations in reverse order: simplify each side first, then isolate the variable.

💡 Worked Example
Solve $$3x + 5 = 20$$.

Subtract 5 from both sides:
$$3x = 15$$

Divide by 3:
$$x = 5$$

✅ Check
$$3(5) + 5 = 20$$, so the solution is correct.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Do the same operation to both sides.
• Simplify brackets and collect like terms first.
• The goal is to get the variable alone on one side.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Forgetting to change the sign when moving a term to the other side.

notes.heading: Variables on Both Sides
notes.body:
📌 Definition
An equation has variables on both sides when the unknown appears on the left and the right of the equals sign.

🔑 How it works
Collect variable terms on one side and number terms on the other. Choose the side that keeps the variable positive if possible.

💡 Worked Example
Solve $$4x + 7 = 2x + 13$$.

Subtract $$2x$$ from both sides:
$$2x + 7 = 13$$

Subtract 7:
$$2x = 6$$

Divide by 2:
$$x = 3$$

✅ Check
$$4(3) + 7 = 19$$ and $$2(3) + 13 = 19$$.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Move variable terms to the side with the larger coefficient.
• Keep the equation balanced at every step.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Adding variable terms instead of subtracting them.

notes.heading: Equations with Brackets
notes.body:
📌 Definition
Brackets show that a number or expression multiplies every term inside the bracket.

🔑 How it works
Expand brackets first, then collect like terms and solve.

💡 Worked Example
Solve $$2(3x - 4) = 10$$.

Expand:
$$6x - 8 = 10$$

Add 8:
$$6x = 18$$

Divide by 6:
$$x = 3$$

✅ Check
$$2(3(3) - 4) = 2(5) = 10$$.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Multiply the outside term by each term inside the bracket.
• Watch negative signs carefully.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Only multiplying the first term inside the bracket.

notes.heading: Understanding Inequalities
notes.body:
📌 Definition
An inequality compares two expressions using <, >, ≤, or ≥.

🔑 Key Concept
The symbols mean:
< less than
> greater than
≤ less than or equal to
≥ greater than or equal to

💡 Worked Example
Write "x is at least 7" as an inequality:
$$x \ge 7$$

Write "y is fewer than 12" as an inequality:
$$y < 12$$

📎 Key Points to Remember
• "At least" and "minimum" use ≥.
• "At most" and "maximum" use ≤.
• "More than" uses >; "less than" uses <.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Confusing "at least" with ≤. "At least 10" means 10 or more, so use ≥.

notes.heading: Solving Linear Inequalities
notes.body:
📌 Definition
Solving an inequality means finding all values of the variable that make the inequality true.

🔑 How it works
Solve inequalities just like equations, except reverse the inequality sign when multiplying or dividing by a negative number.

💡 Worked Example
Solve $$-2x + 6 > 10$$.

Subtract 6:
$$-2x > 4$$

Divide by -2 and flip the sign:
$$x < -2$$

✅ Check
Try $$x = -3$$:
$$-2(-3) + 6 = 12 > 10$$, which is true.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Add or subtract any number without flipping.
• Flip only when multiplying or dividing by a negative.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Forgetting to reverse the sign when dividing by a negative number.

notes.heading: Inequalities on a Number Line

illustration.alt: Number line showing x greater than -1 with an open circle and right shading, and x less than or equal to 2 with a closed circle and left shading.
illustration.caption: Use an open circle for strict inequalities and a closed circle for inclusive inequalities.

notes.body:
📌 Definition
A number line shows the set of solutions to an inequality.

🔑 How it works
Use an open circle for < or > and a closed circle for ≤ or ≥. Shade in the direction of the solutions.

💡 Worked Example
Show $$x > -1$$ on a number line:
Draw a line, mark -1 with an open circle, and shade everything to the right.

Show $$x \le 2$$ on a number line:
Mark 2 with a closed circle and shade to the left.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Open circle means the endpoint is not included.
• Closed circle means the endpoint is included.
• Shade right for greater than, left for less than.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Using a closed circle for strict inequalities such as $$x > 3$$.

notes.heading: Word Problems with Equations and Inequalities
notes.body:
📌 Definition
A word problem describes a real situation that can be translated into an equation or inequality.

🔑 How it works
1. Define the variable.
2. Write an equation or inequality from the sentence.
3. Solve and interpret the answer in context.

💡 Worked Example
A rectangle has a perimeter of 30 cm. Its length is 5 cm more than its width. Find the width.

Let width = w. Then length = w + 5.
Perimeter equation:
$$2w + 2(w + 5) = 30$$

Simplify:
$$4w + 10 = 30$$
$$4w = 20$$
$$w = 5$$ cm

✅ Check
Length = 10 cm, perimeter = 2(5) + 2(10) = 30 cm.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Always state what the variable represents.
• Check that your answer makes sense in the problem.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Ignoring units or giving an impossible answer such as a negative length.

flashcards.term: Open circle on a number line
flashcards.definition: Shows that the endpoint value is not included in the solution set.
flashcards.example: $x > 3$ is drawn with an open circle at 3.

flashcards.term: Closed circle on a number line
flashcards.definition: Shows that the endpoint value is included in the solution set.
flashcards.example: $x \le 5$ is drawn with a closed circle at 5.

questions.explanation: Subtract 4 from both sides to get 2x = 10, then divide by 2 to get x = 5.
Add 3 to both sides to get 5x = 20, then divide by 5 to get x = 4.
Expand to get 3x + 6 = 21, subtract 6 to get 3x = 15, then divide by 3 to get x = 5.
Subtract x from both sides and subtract 5 to get 3x = 9, then divide by 3 to get x = 3.
Subtract 7 from both sides to get -2x = -6, then divide by -2 to get x = 3.
Expand to get 6x - 2 = 4x + 8, subtract 4x and add 2 to get 2x = 10, so x = 5.

questions.stem: Which inequality means "x is at most 8"?
questions.explanation: "At most 8" means 8 is allowed and any value below it, so the correct symbol is ≤.
Divide both sides by -4 and reverse the inequality sign to get x ≥ -5.

questions.stem: Which description matches $x > -2$ on a number line?
questions.explanation: The > symbol means -2 is not included, so use an open circle, and values greater than -2 lie to the right.

questions.stem: A number is doubled and then 5 is added. The result is 23. What is the number?

questions.stem: A rectangle's length is 4 cm more than its width. The perimeter is 32 cm. Find the width.
questions.explanation: Let width be w. Then 2w + 2(w + 4) = 32, which simplifies to 4w + 8 = 32, so w = 6 cm.
